units.text: Three ordinary choices quietly shape your net worth, and none of them feels dramatic.
Start with time. Say you invest $300 every month, assuming an average 8 percent annual return.
If you start today, that portfolio grows to about $447,108 after 30 years.
But if you wait ten years before you start, contributing the same $300 a month for the remaining 20 years, you end up with only about $176,706.
That ten year delay costs you $270,402.
At a 5% rate, you will pay back about $33,968 in total.
At a 9% rate, you will pay back about $37,365 in total.
That gap in the rate costs you an extra $3,397.
Imagine you invest $20,000 and leave it alone for 25 years, earning about 7 percent a year before costs.
With a fund charging 0.1 percent a year, you would end up with about $106,041.
With a fund charging 1 percent a year, you would end up with about $85,837.
Start early, borrow carefully, and check every fee before you commit.
